newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BAKER JAILED FOR FOOD POISONING AT SCHOOL.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BAKER JAILED FOR FOOD POISONING AT SCHOOL.

text.p: A Polish court on Monday sentenced a pastry shop owner to two years in jail for causing the food poisoning of 140 teachers and children, PAP news agency said.
The municipal court in the north Poland city of Olsztyn also barred the man, named only as Andrzej R., from working as a pastry chef for six years, the agency added.
Two years ago, staff and pupils of an Olsztyn school celebrating Teacher's Day got salmonella food poisoning after consuming the baker's cream cakes, it reported.

Cheap, cracked eggs were used to make them amid appalling, sanitary conditions, because the shop's owner, a licenced pastry chef for 18 years, skimped on cleaning compounds. The place was a filthy mess, crawling with insects, PAP reported.
Recalling the pride a man's craft should entail, the judge said that for Andrzej R. money was all that counted.
"This is not a criminal case. It is about betraying one's own life's vocation," PAP quoted the judge as saying.
According to Polish legal custom, courts frequently decide not to reveal the surnames of people involved in court cases.
